summary: Review 27 requirements from the call and one separately sourced tracker model-policy item. Trading reliability comes first, followed by backtesting and paper history, then the AI improvement pilot. Linked development work still needs verification against these outcomes.

priority_legend.P1: Core workflows, coordination and existing model routing

review_notes: Items marked Comments needed contain an important choice to confirm.
Checks marked proposed verification are suggested ways to demonstrate the result; added safeguards are identified separately.
Timestamps identify approximate call sections. ROUTE-001 comes from earlier user instructions.
The improvement percentages are research aspirations to evaluate, not guaranteed results.
Merged or open tracker work remains linked until the requested behaviour is revalidated.

requirements.title: Complete every required protective exit
requirements.problem: A reported stop-loss closed only part of a position, leaving the rest for manual intervention.
requirements.requested_outcome: Complete and confirm the intended protective exit for the affected strategy’s full remaining quantity, without closing another strategy’s position.
requirements.observed_incident: Reported incomplete protective exit; the cause is not verified.
hypothesized_causes: Shared handling, delayed updates and deployment changes were discussed as possible explanations.

evidence.summary: The caller reported that half the intended quantity had not exited.
The caller emphasized that missed stop-loss execution was unacceptable.

acceptance_checks.text: Check that the reported partial-exit case closes the full intended quantity in a controlled test.
Test partial fills, delayed updates and an interrupted exit, including how the remaining quantity is identified and handled.
Distinguish an exit request, a partial fill and a confirmed full exit.

requirements.title: Prevent one strategy from blocking another valid entry
requirements.problem: Similar strategies operating together were reported to miss valid entries, including on previously working accounts.
requirements.requested_outcome: Process each eligible strategy entry independently and explain any valid rejection or delay.
requirements.observed_incident: Reported missed entries when similar strategies operated together.
hypothesized_causes: The other strategy’s quantity or a delayed update may have affected a safety check.

evidence.summary: The speakers described missed entries when similar strategies ran together and committed to correcting the platform behaviour.

acceptance_checks.text: Test simultaneous entries for two strategies on the same instrument and account, with either strategy confirmed first.
Confirm both eligible entries complete once each; retain real safety checks and clear reasons for rejection.
Repeat across more than one affected configuration.

requirements.title: Keep even identical strategies independent
requirements.problem: Strategies that share an account and instrument must not interfere with one another.
requirements.requested_outcome: Keep each strategy independent even when its entry rules, exits, stops, quantity and account are identical to another strategy.

evidence.summary: The client asked for completely identical strategies to behave independently.
The client said one strategy’s stop-loss must not exit another strategy.

acceptance_checks.text: Test two identical strategies together and track their entries, quantities, protection and exits separately.
An exit in one strategy must not close or remove protection from the other.
Repeat with different stop-loss and exit rules and newly added similar strategies.

requirements.decision_needed: Approve independent behaviour; choose the technical design after investigating.

requirements.title: Send each strategy the updates it needs
requirements.problem: A speaker suggested that one strategy may receive an update that another also needs, leaving the second unable to act.
requirements.requested_outcome: Deliver relevant updates to every intended strategy, with each acting only on its own position and instructions.
hypothesized_causes: One strategy consuming an update needed by another was suggested but not proven.
proposed_approaches: The call suggested distributing relevant updates to both strategies for independent assessment.

evidence.summary: The conversation proposed giving both strategy versions the relevant incoming update for independent assessment.
The client asked that each strategy check whether an update belongs to it.

acceptance_checks.text: Show that each intended strategy receives the relevant update and identifies its own action.
Test delayed, repeated and out-of-order updates without missed actions or duplicate orders.
Distributing an update to several strategies must not create extra broker orders.

requirements.decision_needed: Validate the cause before choosing an update-routing design.

requirements.title: Match shared broker positions to the correct strategies
requirements.problem: The broker may show a combined position while the platform needs to know each strategy’s share.
requirements.requested_outcome: Keep each strategy’s quantity accurate when several strategies share an account and instrument, while preserving safety checks.
hypothesized_causes: Combined broker quantity and shared processing were discussed as possible sources of interference.
proposed_approaches: Keep an accurate platform record of each strategy’s actions and quantity.

evidence.summary: The speakers noted that the broker does not label a combined position by strategy version and discussed distinguishing the strategies within the platform.

acceptance_checks.text: Match the combined broker quantity to the quantities assigned to the relevant strategies during entries, partial fills and exits.
Test a manual exit without assigning its effect to an unrelated strategy.
Keep any unexplained difference visible instead of assuming that all positions are closed or bypassing a safety check.

requirements.title: Test all important similar-strategy combinations
requirements.problem: The client asked for a broader review instead of repeatedly repairing only the latest symptom.
requirements.requested_outcome: Test the meaningful combinations of similar strategies before declaring the reliability work complete.

evidence.summary: The client requested a broad review of similar-strategy combinations and additional possible failures.
The developer described the intended result as reliable operation for newly added similar strategies too.

acceptance_checks.text: Cover identical and different rules, simultaneous and staggered entries, both update orders, partial exits, manual exits and multiple accounts.
Add a repeatable check for every reproduced incident, including missed entries and incomplete exits.
Check correctness and response time under realistic delays; efficiency must not hide failures.

requirements.title: Review how each change affects existing features
requirements.problem: The client wants likely interactions considered before a change creates another operational problem.
requirements.requested_outcome: Before implementation, identify how the change could affect existing behaviour and how existing behaviour could affect the new change.

evidence.summary: The client asked for a two-way impact review between a new change and previously implemented behaviour.

acceptance_checks.text: Record the affected workflows and likely interaction problems.
Check previous supported behaviour as well as the new feature’s expected result.

requirements.title: Finish testing before declaring readiness
requirements.problem: An earlier testing cycle was described as stopping with unresolved issues.
requirements.requested_outcome: Complete the required integration and regression checks before declaring readiness. Delay the change when more review or testing is needed.

evidence.summary: The call described an earlier testing cycle leaving issues unresolved.
The speakers emphasized completing integration testing and preserving existing behaviour.
The client allowed delaying a change by a day if more review or testing was needed.

acceptance_checks.text: Report the checks completed, results and anything unfinished.
Do not declare readiness while required checks or critical failures remain unresolved.
Explain any delay and give a revised readiness checkpoint.

requirements.decision_needed: Allow extra time when a specific change needs more review or testing.

requirements.title: Give a clear readiness decision for the trading fixes
requirements.problem: The client said continuing on the platform was not worthwhile while the reliability problem remained unresolved.
requirements.requested_outcome: Prioritize the similar-strategy fixes and give an evidence-based readiness decision before the next intended trading session.

evidence.summary: Reliability fixes were given high priority, with a weekend commitment and concern about continuing while unresolved.
The developer said readiness would be communicated before the intended Monday session.

acceptance_checks.text: State what was reproduced, fixed and tested, and what remains unresolved.
Give the responsible operator the evidence needed for the trading-readiness decision.

timing.note: Original call timing. Confirm current status and the next agreed date.

requirements.title: Agree a maintenance and testing window
requirements.problem: Unclear trading-end times were delaying the start of a full testing cycle.
requirements.requested_outcome: Have the operator notify the developer when trading has finished or is paused, then agree when maintenance and testing can begin.

evidence.summary: The client offered to report when trading had finished or been paused, and the developer agreed this would help.
Earlier notice was linked to completing the full testing cycle.

acceptance_checks.text: Agree who announces the available window, who confirms it and when testing is expected to finish.
Before disruptive work, check open positions and pending orders separately; a pause alone does not prove they are closed.

requirements.decision_needed: Agree the window procedure and responsible roles; the call did not establish a fixed daily time.

requirements.title: Show whether backtests match the comparable paper history
requirements.problem: The client reported mismatches, while another speaker said the periods matched. The disagreement needs a shared comparison.
requirements.requested_outcome: Compare the same strategy, period and assumptions across the available July, August and September examples; explain or correct differences.
requirements.observed_incident: The client reported mismatches; another speaker reported matching results. The shared evidence needs review.

evidence.summary: The client reported older-period backtest results that did not match.
Another speaker said the July, August and September comparisons already matched.

acceptance_checks.text: Agree the exact strategy version, dates, configuration, data and execution assumptions.
Compare entries, exits, quantities, outcomes and summary results, listing every unexplained difference.
Explain valid differences and missing data; a matching total alone is not enough.

requirements.decision_needed: Identify the exact strategy version, comparison report, dates, data and settings to use as the shared baseline.
requirements.comment_prompt: Identify the exact strategy version, comparison report, dates, data and settings to use as the shared baseline.

requirements.title: Validate longer histories and more than one strategy
requirements.problem: A few matching recent trades from one strategy did not address the client’s concern about older periods and other strategies.
requirements.requested_outcome: Use representative strategies with a larger available paper history and compare older as well as recent periods.

evidence.summary: The client asked for a larger available trade history and more than one strategy, rather than a few matching recent examples.

acceptance_checks.text: Agree a representative strategy set, including an available history of roughly 30 to 50 trades as requested.
Include the disputed older period and a second strategy or configuration; state actual coverage and missing data.

requirements.decision_needed: Confirm the representative strategy set and the older-period history to test.
requirements.comment_prompt: Confirm the representative strategy set and the older-period history to test.

requirements.title: Restore usable paper-trade history and filters
requirements.problem: The user reported being unable to select an account or strategy and unable to see earlier paper-trade results.
requirements.requested_outcome: Allow the user to choose an authorized account and strategy and reliably open its available paper-trade history.
requirements.observed_incident: The user reported unavailable filters and history during the call.
hypothesized_causes: An update in progress was offered as the explanation; actual data loss was not established.

evidence.summary: During the call, the user could not select an account or strategy.
The user reported being unable to see a previous paper-trade result.

acceptance_checks.text: Check both selectors and open a known completed paper-trade result.
After an update or refresh, the same available selections and results remain usable.
Show the difference between no matching data, a loading failure and maintenance.

requirements.title: Share the exact comparison reports for review
requirements.problem: The client did not know which report to inspect when the speakers disagreed about matching results.
requirements.requested_outcome: Provide the relevant comparison report with enough detail for the client to identify and review it.

evidence.summary: The client requested a message identifying the exact report to inspect.

acceptance_checks.text: Provide a report link or clear identifier, strategy version, period and concise explanation of the result.
Confirm the intended reviewer can open it; keep detailed account information in the private report.

requirements.title: Make supported strategies usable in backtesting and paper trading
requirements.problem: The client could not continue strategy development because these workflows were not dependable.
requirements.requested_outcome: Allow the user to run the supported strategy set in backtesting and paper trading and inspect completed results.

evidence.summary: The client asked to be able to backtest any supported strategy that evening; the response included paper trading.

acceptance_checks.text: Run each agreed supported strategy through the relevant workflow and open its result.
Explain unsupported settings or insufficient history instead of silently omitting a result.

timing.note: Original call timing. Confirm current status and the next agreed date.

requirements.title: Plan time for incidents and remaining delivery work
requirements.problem: Operational issues were repeatedly displacing the remaining work, especially backtesting.
requirements.requested_outcome: Provide a realistic plan for urgent fixes and the remaining agreed modules, with owners and checkpoints.

evidence.summary: The client asked that incident work not repeatedly interrupt the remaining development work.
The client asked for more time to be allocated to getting the platform usable.

acceptance_checks.text: List incident work and remaining delivery work with owners and checkpoints.
Explain any capacity conflict and revised sequence so other agreed work does not disappear.

requirements.decision_needed: Agree owners and capacity; no staffing count or budget was decided.

requirements.title: Give a concrete status update and call-back
requirements.problem: The client asked for timely contact and enough detail to know what had been resolved and which tools were usable.
requirements.requested_outcome: Notify the client when the reliability work is ready and give the agreed update on findings, fixes, tool availability and next steps.

evidence.summary: The developer promised a message when the reliability issue was resolved.
The client requested an evening call explaining tool availability, findings and the next correction step.

acceptance_checks.text: Distinguish diagnosed, fixed, tested, usable and still blocked.
State which backtesting and paper-trading functions the client can use and the next checkpoint.
Agree the update owner and current call-back time.

phrases: that evening, before the speaker’s engagement
timing.note: Original call timing. Confirm current status and the next agreed date.

requirements.title: Provide a clear strategy-improvement workspace
requirements.problem: The client wants a practical way to improve an existing strategy beyond a general chat or standalone backtest.
requirements.requested_outcome: Provide a workspace where the user selects an existing strategy and baseline history, then asks for evaluated improvements in plain language.

evidence.summary: The client requested a strategy-improvement module or tab and a facility to select an existing strategy.

acceptance_checks.text: The user can select a strategy and see which baseline and history the analysis uses.
Results explain the proposed change, measured comparison and limitations clearly.

requirements.decision_needed: Should the pilot be the first step toward a dedicated improvement tab, or is the skill/chat experience sufficient?
requirements.comment_prompt: Should the pilot be the first step toward a dedicated improvement tab, or is the skill/chat experience sufficient?

requirements.title: Keep the supplied strategy entries fixed
requirements.problem: The client has already developed the entry logic and wants AI to improve what happens after entry.
requirements.requested_outcome: Use the supplied complete strategy and history as the baseline. Keep entry rules and entry points unchanged while evaluating exits.

evidence.summary: The client repeatedly said to leave entries untouched and offered the complete strategy and inputs.

acceptance_checks.text: Keep entry logic and the same baseline entry set in every candidate.
Record the strategy version, settings and dataset so the comparison can be repeated.
Make missing or excluded data visible; do not quietly remove entries to improve results.

requirements.decision_needed: Entries were repeatedly fixed in the request, but a later example used fewer entries. Confirm that every entry must remain, or explain any separately intended filtering.
requirements.comment_prompt: Entries were repeatedly fixed in the request, but a later example used fewer entries. Confirm that every entry must remain, or explain any separately intended filtering.

requirements.title: Research exit changes that reduce losses and preserve winners
requirements.problem: The client is manually trying indicators and exit rules and wants AI to perform the research and comparison work.
requirements.requested_outcome: Explore approved indicators, exit conditions, stops, trailing stops and targets after the fixed entries, seeking smaller losses while retaining profitable runs where possible.

evidence.summary: The client asked AI to explore indicators and exits that reduce losses while allowing profitable moves to continue.
The client invited experiments with different indicators and exit conditions.

acceptance_checks.text: List each candidate’s allowed changes and the reason for trying them.
Evaluate candidates using the same baseline data and assumptions, including unsuccessful attempts.
Keep proposed changes as research drafts for review before adopting them in live strategies.

requirements.title: Evaluate the 80% / 20% / 100% aspiration
requirements.problem: The client described desired effects on winning and losing trades; feasibility has not been established.
requirements.requested_outcome: On an agreed fixed dataset, aim to leave at least 80% of baseline winners unaffected, allow up to 20% to be affected, and change exits for all baseline losers so losses are reduced. Report feasibility and trade-offs.

evidence.summary: The client described the 80% winner-preservation, 20% affected-winner and 100% losing-trade aspiration.

acceptance_checks.text: Agree what unaffected, affected and loss reduced mean before measuring them.
Show original winners preserved or changed, and original losers improved, unchanged or worsened, with counts and percentages.
Report whether the aspiration was achieved and the best observed trade-off if it was not.

requirements.decision_needed: Define unaffected, affected and loss reduced, and state the acceptable trade-off if the 80% / 20% / 100% aspiration is not feasible.
requirements.comment_prompt: Define unaffected, affected and loss reduced, and state the acceptable trade-off if the 80% / 20% / 100% aspiration is not feasible.

requirements.title: Show a repeatable comparison with the original strategy
requirements.problem: The client wants measured improvement and an explanation of changes, not just suggestions for indicators.
requirements.requested_outcome: Compare the original strategy and each candidate using return or ROI, win rate, risk/reward and individual changed outcomes on the same sample.

evidence.summary: The client wanted an explained comparison showing whether overall return, win rate and risk/reward improved.

acceptance_checks.text: Show original and candidate metrics with the period, dataset and calculation assumptions.
Show which outcomes improved, worsened or stayed the same while preserving fixed entries.
Use consistent cost and slippage assumptions, and test a separate period where sufficient data is available.
Report no improvement when appropriate and make unsuccessful attempts visible.

requirements.decision_needed: Clarify the smaller entry-count example. The example of 1:2 risk/reward and a win rate above 50% is not a fixed target.
requirements.comment_prompt: Confirm how the smaller entry-count example should be interpreted while preserving the agreed entry rules.

requirements.title: Deliver the reusable skill and ready-made prompt
requirements.problem: The client should not need to create a technical prompt for every improvement request.
requirements.requested_outcome: Package the agreed improvement workflow as a runnable skill with a ready-made prompt and simple instructions.

evidence.summary: The developer offered a reusable skill and ready-made prompt.

acceptance_checks.text: Provide a saved skill or prompt that collects the required strategy and data and preserves the agreed entry lock.
Explain where to run it and demonstrate a complete run through to the comparison report.

requirements.title: Send a one-strategy pilot for feedback
requirements.problem: The client has an existing strategy available to try the proposed improvement workflow.
requirements.requested_outcome: Deliver a pilot for one agreed strategy, let the client try the chat or skill flow, and collect feedback before expanding it.

evidence.summary: The developer offered to send a one-strategy pilot, and the client said a strategy was already available to try.

acceptance_checks.text: Agree the pilot strategy privately and demonstrate its complete workflow with plain instructions.
Record feedback and whether the experience meets the client’s improvement needs.
Keep pilot results clearly separate from live trading.

requirements.decision_needed: Confirm the exact pilot strategy version, history period, dataset and baseline settings.
requirements.comment_prompt: Confirm the exact pilot strategy version, history period, dataset and baseline settings.

requirements.title: Reduce repeated manual strategy experiments
requirements.problem: The client repeats exit experiments and backtests and wants the system to take over this repetitive research.
requirements.requested_outcome: Reuse the workflow across approved strategies and measure the manual effort and elapsed time it saves.

evidence.summary: The client described repeated manual backtests and hoped the system could reduce an improvement cycle to a day or a few days.

acceptance_checks.text: Measure the pilot’s elapsed time and the manual steps it replaces.
Run the next strategy without rewriting the research instructions.
Agree a limit for experiments and a progress update so research does not continue indefinitely.

requirements.decision_needed: The hoped-for one-day or few-day cycle is an aspiration; agree a measurable pilot target.

requirements.title: Demonstrate the current Jarvis chat capability
requirements.problem: The developer said the intelligence already existed in chat, while the client had not yet seen practical AI use in this workflow.
requirements.requested_outcome: Demonstrate the current chat with a selected strategy and real available history, separating what works now from the proposed improvement workspace.

evidence.summary: The developer suggested trying the existing Jarvis chat and said the intelligence was already available.

acceptance_checks.text: Show an answer grounded in the chosen strategy and its data rather than generic advice.
Identify missing analysis or reporting capabilities and connect them to the pilot work.

requirements.decision_needed: Verify the existing capability before treating it as delivered.

requirements.title: Verify the claimed Astra 6 and Fable 5.1 adoption
requirements.problem: The developer said these models had already been incorporated, but the call provided no configuration or run evidence.
requirements.requested_outcome: Verify that adoption claim in the intended product or workflow and show which model actually handles each relevant capability.

evidence.summary: The developer named Astra 6 and Fable 5.1 and said they had already been incorporated.

acceptance_checks.text: Check the configured and actually used model identities and demonstrate a relevant successful invocation of each.
Distinguish development tools from the customer-facing platform and chat.
Report anything unavailable or unverified rather than treating a conversational claim as proof.

requirements.decision_needed: Verify model adoption separately from the previously requested tracker-routing policy.

requirements.title: Verify the existing tracker’s model policy across both tools
requirements.problem: Earlier instructions asked the tracker to use Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra together, continue through genuine availability limits, and behave consistently in Codex and Claude Code.
requirements.requested_outcome: Verify the existing tracker work: prefer Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra together. Select the next-best model automatically only when a preferred model is actually unavailable or rate-limited, not for convenience while it remains usable. Keep the workflow and result checks consistent in Codex and Claude Code.

source.label: Earlier tracker discussion, outside this call

evidence.summary: The user asked for both preferred models, automatic fallback only for genuine model unavailability or limits, and a similar workflow in Codex and Claude Code.
evidence.source_label: Earlier user instructions, not the call transcript

acceptance_checks.text: Verify the configured model identities and show both preferred models taking part in their intended roles when available.
Demonstrate fallback for a real or controlled availability/rate-limit failure; record which preferred model was unavailable and why the alternative was selected.
Confirm the tracker does not choose an alternative merely for convenience while the preferred model is usable, and returns to the preferred model when it becomes usable.
Run the same representative tracker task in Codex and Claude Code and compare the workflow, checkpoints and completed result.

requirements.decision_needed: Confirm any remaining role or fallback-order choices against the existing tracker configuration. The requested names are preferences; their exact model IDs and current availability still need verification.

decisions.title: Defer the unspecified UI requests
decisions.detail: The client deferred several UI points while reliability and backtesting remained unresolved. Their details still need a separate discussion.

decisions.title: Allow time for proper review
decisions.detail: A change may be delayed by a day when it needs more impact review or testing. This is flexibility for a particular change.

decisions.detail: Entries were repeatedly fixed in the request, but a later example used fewer entries. Confirm that every entry must remain, or explain any separately intended filtering.

decisions.title: Define the improvement targets
decisions.detail: Define unaffected, affected and loss reduced, and state the acceptable trade-off if the 80% / 20% / 100% aspiration is not feasible.

decisions.title: Agree the pilot and final interface
decisions.detail: Should the pilot be the first step toward a dedicated improvement tab, or is the skill/chat experience sufficient?

decisions.title: Agree the comparison dataset
decisions.detail: Confirm the exact strategy versions, comparison report, period, data and settings from the private source records.

decisions.title: Agree current owners and dates
decisions.detail: The call’s today, evening and Monday references are historical. Confirm current status, owners and the next dates.

decisions.title: Review the added verification safeguards
decisions.detail: Review the proposed checks for consistent data and costs, separate-period testing where possible, research drafts, and checking open positions before maintenance.

decisions.title: Investigate before choosing a technical fix
decisions.detail: Shared processing, update timing and position matching were suggested explanations. Verify the cause before selecting the design.

decisions.detail: Past pauses and account changes describe the incident history; they are not new operating instructions.

decisions.title: Keep illustrative metrics as examples
decisions.detail: The example of 1:2 risk/reward and a win rate above 50% is not an agreed target. Illustrative trade counts do not override the entry lock.

decisions.detail: Verify the call’s model-adoption claim separately from the earlier tracker-routing instruction in ROUTE-001.
